newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi to keep 5 yen annual dividend in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi to keep 5 yen annual dividend in 1996/97.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd expects to keep its annual dividend in the year to March 31, 1997 unchanged from five yen in the previous year, Yamaichi Vice President Ryuji Shirai told a news conference on Wednesday.
Yamaichi said earlier on Wednesday that it would post a parent net loss of 110 billion yen in 1996/97 as a result of the payment of 150 billion yen in financial support to its Yamaichi Finance unit.
The securities house is one of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages.
Yamaichi said in a statement that it would include all of the 150 billion yen in aid as an extraordinary loss in its 1996/97 parent earnings.

The decision to provide the support was made in order to maintain Yamaichi's credibility and increase its competitiveness by immediately dealing with the problem loans held by Yamaichi Finance, the statement said.
Shirai said Yamaichi expects extraordinary profits of about 24 billion yen in 1996/97, partly through the sale of shareholdings.
The company previously said it would post parent net profit of 16 billion yen in 1996/97.
Even after providing the financial aid, Yamaichi will have a capital safety ratio of between 220 to 230 percent, Shirai said, without elaborating.
The securities house was not considering issuing corporate bonds, Shirai said.
